subject.title: [security] OVH provider client forwards signed credential headers across cross-origin redirects

question: Should the OVH provider adopt the same credential-destination redirect guard used by other credential-bearing provider clients, and should it be exact-origin or broader OVH-authority only?
rationale: The source path is clear, but changing redirect handling for a credentialed external provider is a security-boundary choice that may affect legitimate OVH redirect behavior.

options.title: Fix as exact-origin security bug
options.body: Reject redirects whose scheme, hostname, or effective port differs from the configured OVH endpoint, matching the documented destination principle.

options.title: Allow only OVH-authority redirects
options.body: Permit redirects within a maintainer-defined OVH host policy, but add tests proving no lower-trust origin receives signed headers.

options.title: Defer as trusted-provider risk
options.body: Leave behavior unchanged only if maintainers explicitly accept first-party OVH redirect trust for signed request headers.

recommendation.title: Fix as exact-origin security bug
recommendation.body: Reject redirects whose scheme, hostname, or effective port differs from the configured OVH endpoint, matching the documented destination principle.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete merged the OVH provider work and authored adjacent provider redirect hardening, making him the best available routing owner for the boundary choice.
